questions.stem: A provider documents a 'nephrectomy.' Breaking the term into its components, what does the suffix -ectomy indicate?

options.text: Surgical removal or excision of the structure named by the root
Creation of a new permanent opening
Surgical repair of the structure
Visual examination of the interior of the structure

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** The suffix -ectomy means surgical excision/removal, so nephr/ectomy is removal of a kidney. Why the others are wrong: **B** creation of a new opening is -ostomy; **C** surgical repair is -plasty (or -rrhaphy for suture repair); **D** visual examination with a scope is -scopy.

questions.stem: In standard anatomical position, a structure described as 'proximal' on a limb is:

options.text: Nearer to the point of attachment to the trunk
Farther from the point of attachment to the trunk
Toward the midline of the body
Toward the back surface of the body

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Proximal means nearer the trunk or point of origin of a limb (the elbow is proximal to the wrist). Why the others are wrong: **B** farther from attachment is distal; **C** toward the midline is medial; **D** toward the back is posterior (dorsal).

questions.stem: A pathology report uses the prefix 'inter-' and the prefix 'intra-' in different findings. What is the correct distinction between them?

options.text: Inter- means between structures; intra- means within a structure
Inter- means within a structure; intra- means between structures
Both mean 'around' but at different scales
Inter- means below; intra- means above

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Inter- = between (intercostal = between the ribs); intra- = within (intramuscular = within a muscle). Why the others are wrong: **B** reverses the two prefixes; **C** 'around' is peri-, not these prefixes; **D** below is infra-/sub- and above is supra-/epi-.

questions.stem: Which two terms correctly pair a combining form with the body system it primarily relates to? (Select two.)

options.text: Hepat/o — the liver (digestive/hepatobiliary system)
Pneum/o — the kidneys (urinary system)
Oste/o — bone (musculoskeletal system)
Cardi/o — the stomach (digestive system)

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, C):** Hepat/o refers to the liver and oste/o refers to bone, each matched to the correct system. Why the others are wrong: **B** pneum/o refers to lung/air, not the kidneys (nephr/o or ren/o); **D** cardi/o refers to the heart, not the stomach (gastr/o).

questions.stem: A note states the lesion is on the 'plantar' surface of the foot and 'dorsal' aspect of the hand. These terms respectively describe the:

options.text: Sole of the foot and the back of the hand
Top of the foot and the palm of the hand
Inner ankle and the wrist crease
Heel of the foot and the fingertips

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Plantar refers to the sole (bottom) of the foot, and dorsal refers to the back of the hand. Why the others are wrong: **B** describes dorsal foot and palmar hand, the opposites; **C** names the medial ankle and volar wrist, unrelated terms; **D** the heel is the calcaneal region and fingertips are distal phalanges.

questions.stem: Place the basic steps of correctly assigning an ICD-10-CM diagnosis code in the proper order, from first to last.

options.text: Locate the main term for the condition in the Alphabetic Index
Read and apply any subterms, notes, and cross-references under the Index entry
Verify the candidate code in the Tabular List, following all instructional notes
Assign the complete code to the highest level of specificity (including required characters)

questions.explanation: The correct sequence is: find the main term in the Alphabetic Index, then apply subterms/notes and cross-references, then verify the candidate code in the Tabular List honoring every instructional note, and finally assign the complete code to its highest specificity. This order matters because the Index only points to a candidate code; a coder must never code straight from the Index, and the Tabular List is where laterality, seventh characters, and excludes/includes notes are confirmed before the code is finalized.

questions.stem: An ICD-10-CM Tabular entry shows the convention 'Code first' beneath a manifestation code. This instructional note tells the coder to:

options.text: Sequence the underlying etiology/condition before this code
Assign only this code and ignore the underlying condition
Sequence this code first as the principal diagnosis
Add a seventh character to indicate the encounter type

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** 'Code first' is a sequencing instruction signaling an etiology/manifestation relationship—the underlying condition is coded and sequenced before the manifestation code. Why the others are wrong: **B** both codes are reported, not just one; **C** the manifestation is sequenced second, not first; **D** seventh characters relate to encounter/episode, a separate convention.

questions.stem: A patient is seen in the office for follow-up of a healing fracture during the normal recovery phase. Which seventh-character value generally applies to this routine aftercare encounter for the fracture?

options.text: D — subsequent encounter (routine healing)
A — initial encounter (active treatment)
S — sequela
X — placeholder character

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** For injuries, seventh character 'D' indicates a subsequent encounter during routine healing/recovery after active treatment has ended. Why the others are wrong: **B** 'A' is used while the patient is still receiving active treatment for the injury; **C** 'S' identifies a sequela (late effect) of the injury, not routine healing; **D** 'X' is a dummy placeholder, not an encounter value.

questions.stem: Within the CPT Surgery section, procedures on the musculoskeletal system are primarily found in which numeric range?

options.text: The 20000 series
The 10000 series
The 40000 series
The 60000 series

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** The musculoskeletal system occupies the 20000 series of CPT Surgery. Why the others are wrong: **B** the 10000 series is the integumentary system; **C** the 40000 series is the digestive system; **D** the 60000 series covers the nervous system, eye, and auditory system.

questions.stem: Which two services are bundled into the CPT surgical package and not reported separately? (Select two.)

options.text: Typical postoperative follow-up care related to the surgery
Local infiltration, metacarpal/digital block, or topical anesthesia by the surgeon
Treatment of a complication requiring a return trip to the operating room
A significant, separately identifiable E/M for an unrelated problem during the global period

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, B):** The surgical package bundles the operation, the surgeon's local/digital-block/topical anesthesia, and typical related postoperative follow-up care. Why the others are wrong: **C** a return to the OR to treat a complication is separately reportable (modifier 78); **D** an unrelated, separately identifiable E/M during the global period is reported separately (modifier 24).

questions.stem: When coding excision of a benign skin lesion in the integumentary section, the size used to select the code is measured as:

options.text: The greatest lesion diameter plus the narrowest margins required for the excision
The lesion diameter only, after fixation in the pathology lab
The length of the final sutured wound
The total surface area in square centimeters

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Excised diameter equals the greatest clinical diameter of the lesion plus the most narrow margin needed on each side, measured before excision. Why the others are wrong: **B** specimens shrink after fixation, so the pre-excision clinical measurement is used; **C** repair (closure) length is coded separately, not used to size the excision; **D** lesion excision is sized by diameter, not square-centimeter area.

questions.stem: A surgeon performs an intermediate wound repair. In CPT, an 'intermediate' repair differs from a 'simple' repair primarily because it includes:

options.text: Layered closure of one or more deeper layers in addition to the skin
Only single-layer closure of the epidermis
Extensive undermining and complex flap creation
Debridement of devitalized tissue down to bone

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Intermediate repair requires layered closure of one or more deeper layers (subcutaneous tissue/superficial fascia) plus the skin. Why the others are wrong: **B** single-layer epidermal/dermal closure defines simple repair; **C** undermining and complex techniques define complex repair; **D** debridement to bone is a separate musculoskeletal-style service, not what distinguishes intermediate repair.

questions.stem: An operative note for laceration repair lists multiple wounds: two intermediate repairs in the same anatomic group and one simple repair in a different group. CPT repair guidelines instruct the coder to:

options.text: Add together the lengths of repairs in the same classification and anatomic group, and report the most complex repair first
Report only the single longest wound and ignore the others
Sum the lengths of all wounds regardless of classification or anatomic site into one code
Code each individual wound separately even when same classification and group

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Lengths of repairs of the same classification (simple/intermediate/complex) and same anatomic grouping are summed, and the most complex repair is listed first. Why the others are wrong: **B** all repairs are reported, not just the longest; **C** you may not combine across different classifications or anatomic groups; **D** wounds in the same classification and group are added together, not coded individually.

questions.stem: In the CPT musculoskeletal section, the terms 'closed treatment' and 'open treatment' of a fracture are distinguished by whether:

options.text: The fracture site is surgically opened/exposed (open) versus not exposed (closed)
The skin over the fracture was lacerated at the time of injury
Anesthesia was general (open) versus local (closed)
Imaging was used during the procedure

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** In CPT, 'open treatment' means the fracture is surgically opened/exposed (or opened remotely) to treat it; 'closed treatment' means the site is not surgically opened. Why the others are wrong: **B** an open vs. closed wound at injury is a clinical injury type, not the CPT treatment definition; **C** anesthesia type does not define the treatment category; **D** imaging guidance does not determine open versus closed.

questions.stem: A diagnostic endoscopy is performed and, during the same session, the surgeon proceeds to a surgical endoscopy. Per CPT endoscopy guidelines, the coder should report:

options.text: The surgical endoscopy, which includes the diagnostic endoscopy
Both the diagnostic and the surgical endoscopy separately
Only the diagnostic endoscopy
Neither, because endoscopies are always bundled into an E/M

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** A surgical endoscopy always includes a diagnostic endoscopy, so only the surgical service is reported when both occur in the same session. Why the others are wrong: **B** reporting both unbundles a service that is inclusive; **C** when a surgical procedure is done, the diagnostic-only code does not capture the work; **D** endoscopies are distinct procedural services, not bundled into E/M.

questions.stem: Procedures of the digestive system in CPT Surgery are organized in which numeric series?

options.text: The 40000 series
The 30000 series
The 50000 series
The 20000 series

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** The digestive system spans the 40000 series of CPT Surgery (mouth through anus, plus the abdomen/peritoneum). Why the others are wrong: **B** the 30000 series is respiratory, cardiovascular, and hemic/lymphatic; **C** the 50000 series is urinary, reproductive, maternity, and endocrine; **D** the 20000 series is musculoskeletal.

questions.stem: During a screening colonoscopy on a Medicare patient, a polyp is found and removed by snare. The procedure converts from screening to therapeutic. Which HCPCS modifier is appropriately appended to indicate the screening that became diagnostic/therapeutic?

options.text: Modifier PT (colorectal cancer screening test converted to a diagnostic/therapeutic procedure)
Modifier 33 only, because the service remains preventive
Modifier 52 for a reduced service
Modifier 59 to unbundle the polypectomy

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** HCPCS modifier PT indicates a colorectal cancer screening that was converted to a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure, affecting beneficiary cost-sharing for Medicare. Why the others are wrong: **B** once a polyp is removed the service is no longer purely preventive, so modifier 33 alone is inappropriate here; **C** modifier 52 signals a reduced service, which did not occur; **D** modifier 59 marks a distinct procedural service, not a screening-to-therapeutic conversion.

questions.stem: Which two statements about CPT add-on codes used in the surgery section are correct? (Select two.)

options.text: They are never reported alone and must accompany a primary procedure
They are typically exempt from modifier 51 (multiple procedures)
They must always be appended with modifier 50 for bilateral
They represent a stand-alone primary procedure on their own

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, B):** Add-on codes describe additional work performed with a primary procedure, are never reported alone, and are exempt from the multiple-procedure modifier 51. Why the others are wrong: **C** modifier 50 applies only to genuinely bilateral procedures, not as a blanket rule for add-ons; **D** an add-on code is by definition not a stand-alone primary procedure.

questions.stem: In CPT, the maternity care and delivery subsection generally bundles 'global obstetric care.' This global package typically includes:

options.text: Antepartum care, delivery, and postpartum care
Only the delivery itself
Only antepartum and postpartum visits, never the delivery
All visits plus any unrelated medical problems during pregnancy

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Global OB care bundles routine antepartum care, the delivery, and postpartum care into one package. Why the others are wrong: **B** the global package is more than the delivery alone; **C** the delivery is part of the global package; **D** unrelated medical problems (e.g., conditions not part of routine maternity care) are reported separately.

questions.stem: A urologist documents a 'cystourethroscopy.' Based on the term, this procedure visualizes the:

options.text: Urinary bladder and urethra
Ureter and renal pelvis only
Gallbladder and bile ducts
Stomach and duodenum

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Cyst/o (bladder) + urethr/o (urethra) + -scopy (visual exam) means endoscopic examination of the bladder and urethra. Why the others are wrong: **B** the ureter and renal pelvis involve uretero/pyelo terms; **C** the gallbladder/bile ducts are cholecyst/o and chol/e terms; **D** the stomach and duodenum are gastr/o and duoden/o terms.

questions.stem: A surgeon begins a planned laparoscopic cholecystectomy but, due to dense adhesions, converts to an open procedure. CPT guidance for a laparoscopic procedure converted to an open procedure is to report:

options.text: Only the open procedure code that was ultimately completed
Both the laparoscopic and open codes for the same organ
Only the laparoscopic code with modifier 53
The laparoscopic code with modifier 22 and the open code

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** When a scope procedure is converted to an open approach, report only the open procedure actually completed (the laparoscopic attempt is not separately billed). Why the others are wrong: **B** reporting both for the same organ unbundles the work; **C** the procedure was completed openly, not discontinued, so modifier 53 is inappropriate; **D** combining a laparoscopic code with the open code double-reports the service.

questions.stem: When a procedure is performed bilaterally and the CPT code descriptor does not already specify 'bilateral,' the coder generally reports it with:

options.text: Modifier 50 (bilateral procedure)
Modifier 59 (distinct procedural service)
Modifier 76 (repeat procedure by same physician)
Modifier 91 (repeat clinical diagnostic lab test)

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Modifier 50 reports a procedure performed bilaterally when the code itself is unilateral or silent on laterality. Why the others are wrong: **B** modifier 59 marks a distinct service, not bilaterality; **C** modifier 76 is for a repeat of the same procedure, not two sides at once; **D** modifier 91 applies to repeated clinical lab tests only.

questions.stem: A physician begins a screening procedure under conscious sedation but discontinues it after the scope is inserted because the patient becomes hemodynamically unstable. To indicate a discontinued procedure after anesthesia/initiation in a facility (outpatient hospital/ASC) setting, the coder uses:

options.text: Modifier 74 (discontinued outpatient procedure after anesthesia administration)
Modifier 53 (discontinued procedure by the physician)
Modifier 52 (reduced services)
Modifier 73 (discontinued before anesthesia administration)

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** In the outpatient hospital/ASC setting, modifier 74 reports a procedure discontinued after anesthesia was administered or the procedure was started. Why the others are wrong: **B** modifier 53 is the physician's professional discontinuation modifier, not the facility modifier; **C** modifier 52 is for a planned reduction in service, not an aborted procedure; **D** modifier 73 applies when the facility procedure is stopped before anesthesia is given.

questions.stem: The nervous system, eye and ocular adnexa, and the auditory system are grouped together in which CPT Surgery numeric series?

options.text: The 60000 series
The 30000 series
The 50000 series
The 10000 series

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** The 60000 series covers the nervous system, the eye and ocular adnexa, and the auditory system. Why the others are wrong: **B** the 30000 series is respiratory, cardiovascular, and hemic/lymphatic; **C** the 50000 series is urinary, reproductive, maternity, and endocrine; **D** the 10000 series is the integumentary system.

questions.stem: Arrange these CPT Surgery body-system subsections in the order their code ranges ascend numerically, from lowest to highest.

options.text: Integumentary system
Musculoskeletal system
Digestive system
Nervous system / eye / auditory

questions.explanation: The correct ascending order is integumentary (10000 series) → musculoskeletal (20000 series) → digestive (40000 series) → nervous/eye/auditory (60000 series). This order matters because CPT Surgery is organized by ascending code ranges that map to body systems; knowing the sequence lets a coder navigate quickly from skin procedures up through the highest-numbered nervous and special-senses procedures.

questions.stem: Under the current CPT office/outpatient E/M guidelines, which two methods may be used to select the level of service? (Select two.)

options.text: Total time spent on the date of the encounter
The level of medical decision making (MDM)
The number of body areas and organ systems examined
The number of prescriptions written during the visit

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, B):** Office/outpatient E/M levels are selected by either total time on the encounter date or the level of medical decision making (MDM). Why the others are wrong: **C** counting body areas/organ systems reflects the older history-and-exam scoring no longer used to set these levels; **D** prescription count is only one input into MDM risk, not a stand-alone selection method.

questions.stem: The three elements that determine the level of medical decision making (MDM) in the current E/M guidelines are the number/complexity of problems, the amount/complexity of data reviewed, and:

options.text: The risk of complications and/or morbidity or mortality of patient management
The number of organ systems examined
The total face-to-face time only
The patient's insurance type

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** MDM is scored on three elements: problems addressed, data reviewed/analyzed, and the risk of complications/morbidity/mortality of management. Why the others are wrong: **B** counting organ systems is part of the legacy exam scoring, not an MDM element; **C** time is an alternative selection method, not an MDM element; **D** insurance type is irrelevant to MDM.

questions.stem: A patient is seen in the emergency department, evaluated, and sent home (not admitted). The patient has not been formally registered as an inpatient or in observation. The correct E/M category to consider is:

options.text: Emergency department services
Initial hospital inpatient or observation care
Subsequent nursing facility care
Home or residence services

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** A patient evaluated in the ED and discharged is reported with emergency department E/M services. Why the others are wrong: **B** initial hospital inpatient/observation applies only if the patient is admitted to that status; **C** nursing facility codes apply to SNF/NF settings; **D** home/residence services apply when the visit occurs in the patient's residence.

questions.stem: A significant, separately identifiable E/M service is performed by the same physician on the same day as a minor procedure with a global period. The modifier appended to the E/M code is:

options.text: Modifier 25
Modifier 57
Modifier 24
Modifier 59

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Modifier 25 identifies a significant, separately identifiable E/M service on the same day as another procedure or service by the same physician. Why the others are wrong: **B** modifier 57 is for an E/M that results in the decision for major surgery; **C** modifier 24 is for an unrelated E/M during a postoperative global period; **D** modifier 59 marks distinct procedural services, not E/M separateness.

questions.stem: An anesthesiologist personally performs anesthesia. The standard formula used to value an anesthesia service is generally:

options.text: (Base units + time units +/- modifying units) multiplied by a conversion factor
Base units only, regardless of time
Time units only, with no base value
The surgeon's fee divided by two

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Anesthesia payment is calculated as base units (for the procedure) plus time units, adjusted by any qualifying/modifying units, multiplied by a conversion factor. Why the others are wrong: **B** ignoring time understates longer cases; **C** omitting base units ignores procedure complexity; **D** anesthesia is valued independently, not as a fraction of the surgeon's fee.

questions.stem: Anesthesia physical status modifier P3 designates a patient who:

options.text: Has severe systemic disease
Is normal and healthy
Is brain-dead and an organ donor
Has mild systemic disease

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** P3 designates a patient with severe systemic disease. Why the others are wrong: **B** a normal healthy patient is P1; **C** a declared brain-dead organ donor is P6; **D** a patient with mild systemic disease is P2.

questions.stem: A radiology service is split between a facility that owns the equipment and a physician who only interprets the image. Which two modifiers correctly capture this professional/technical split? (Select two.)

options.text: Modifier 26 for the professional (interpretation) component
Modifier TC for the technical component
Modifier 51 for the technical component
Modifier 76 for the professional component

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, B):** Modifier 26 reports the professional (physician interpretation) component, and modifier TC reports the technical (equipment/facility) component. Why the others are wrong: **C** modifier 51 indicates multiple procedures, not a technical component; **D** modifier 76 marks a repeat procedure by the same physician, not a professional component.

questions.stem: In a radiology report, a study described as performed 'with and without contrast' means the coder should select a code reflecting:

options.text: Imaging done first without contrast, then again after contrast administration
Two entirely unrelated studies on different days
Contrast taken orally only, never intravascular
A study where contrast was ordered but not given

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** 'With and without contrast' means a noncontrast sequence followed by a contrast-enhanced sequence in the same study. Why the others are wrong: **B** it is a single study, not two unrelated exams on separate days; **C** for CPT radiology purposes, 'with contrast' generally refers to intravascular (or intra-articular/intrathecal) administration, not oral contrast alone; **D** contrast is actually administered, not merely ordered.

questions.stem: In CPT Radiology, the term 'radiological supervision and interpretation' (S&I) refers to:

options.text: The imaging-guidance and interpretation portion that accompanies a procedure, separate from the procedural work itself
The surgical portion of an interventional procedure
The administrative scheduling of imaging studies
The technologist's positioning of the patient only

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** S&I codes capture the supervision of the imaging and the interpretation that accompanies a procedure, reported in addition to the procedural component. Why the others are wrong: **B** the procedural/surgical work is coded separately from S&I; **C** scheduling is administrative and not a billable S&I service; **D** patient positioning by a technologist is not the physician S&I work.

questions.stem: A clinical laboratory repeats the same chemistry test on the same patient on the same day to obtain serial measurements (medically necessary repeats, not to confirm an error). The appropriate modifier is:

options.text: Modifier 91 (repeat clinical diagnostic laboratory test)
Modifier 76 (repeat procedure by same physician)
Modifier 59 (distinct procedural service)
Modifier 90 (reference/outside laboratory)

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Modifier 91 reports a medically necessary repeat of the same clinical diagnostic lab test on the same day. Why the others are wrong: **B** modifier 76 is for repeat procedures/services by the same physician, not lab tests; **C** modifier 59 marks distinct procedural services, not lab repeats; **D** modifier 90 indicates the test was sent to an outside reference lab.

questions.stem: When coding a surgical pathology specimen, the level of service (the gross and microscopic examination tier) is determined principally by:

options.text: The type of specimen and the physician work/complexity associated with examining it
The weight of the specimen in grams
The cost of the reagents used
The time of day the specimen was received

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Surgical pathology levels are assigned by specimen type and the associated physician work/complexity of the gross and microscopic exam. Why the others are wrong: **B** specimen weight is not the basis for the level; **C** reagent cost does not set the pathology level; **D** the time of receipt is irrelevant to code selection.

questions.stem: When administering a single vaccine to a child, CPT generally allows separate reporting of the immunization administration code and the:

options.text: Vaccine/toxoid product code itself
Place-of-service code as a CPT procedure
Diagnosis code as a CPT procedure
Modifier 50 for a bilateral injection

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Immunizations are reported with two components—the administration code and the specific vaccine/toxoid product code. Why the others are wrong: **B** place of service is reported in a separate field, not as a CPT procedure; **C** the diagnosis is an ICD-10-CM code, not a CPT procedure; **D** modifier 50 applies to bilateral anatomic procedures, not a single vaccine injection.

questions.stem: A 12-lead electrocardiogram is documented as 'interpretation and report only' by a cardiologist; a separate facility performed the tracing. The cardiologist should report the ECG with:

options.text: Modifier 26 (professional component)
Modifier TC (technical component)
No modifier, billing the global service
Modifier 52 (reduced services)

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Reporting only the interpretation and report means the physician bills the professional component with modifier 26. Why the others are wrong: **B** modifier TC covers the technical (tracing/equipment) component performed by the facility, not the interpretation; **C** billing globally would claim both components, but the facility did the technical part; **D** modifier 52 is for a reduced service, which does not describe a complete interpretation.

questions.stem: Which two statements about reporting CPT moderate (conscious) sedation are correct? (Select two.)

options.text: Moderate sedation requires monitoring the patient's level of consciousness and physiological status
Intraservice time is a factor in selecting the moderate sedation code
Moderate sedation is the same as general anesthesia rendering the patient fully unconscious
A local anesthetic injection by itself qualifies as moderate sedation

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, B):** Moderate sedation involves monitoring consciousness and physiologic status, and the codes are selected partly by intraservice time and patient age. Why the others are wrong: **C** moderate sedation maintains a depressed but responsive consciousness, unlike general anesthesia; **D** a local anesthetic injection alone is not moderate sedation.

questions.stem: In HCPCS Level II, the alphabetic section that identifies 'drugs administered other than by the oral method' (e.g., injectable and infused drugs) uses codes beginning with which letter?

options.text: J codes
E codes
A codes
L codes

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** HCPCS J codes identify drugs administered other than orally, such as injectables and infusion drugs. Why the others are wrong: **B** E codes are durable medical equipment; **C** A codes include transportation, medical/surgical supplies, and administrative items; **D** L codes are orthotics and prosthetics.

questions.stem: HCPCS modifiers LT and RT are used to indicate that a procedure was performed on the:

options.text: Left side or right side of the body, respectively
Lower or upper extremity, respectively
Lateral or rotational approach, respectively
Long-term or routine basis, respectively

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** LT identifies the left side and RT identifies the right side of the body, specifying laterality for a procedure or item. Why the others are wrong: **B** these are not extremity-level designators; **C** they do not describe a surgical approach; **D** they have nothing to do with duration of care.

questions.stem: When abstracting codes from an operative report, the strongest guidance for selecting the procedure code(s) is to base them on:

options.text: The procedure(s) actually performed as documented in the body of the operative note
The preoperative diagnosis listed at the top of the note only
The title/header of the operative report alone
The anesthesia record's listed procedure

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Codes are abstracted from what was actually performed and documented in the body of the operative report. Why the others are wrong: **B** the preoperative diagnosis may differ from findings and does not establish the procedure; **C** the header may be incomplete or differ from what was done, so it cannot stand alone; **D** the anesthesia record is a supporting document, not the authoritative source for the surgical procedure.

questions.stem: An NCCI Procedure-to-Procedure (PTP) edit pairs two codes with a modifier indicator of '1.' This indicator means:

options.text: The edit may be bypassed with an appropriate modifier when clinically justified
The edit can never be bypassed under any circumstance
The two codes must always be billed together
The column-two code is always paid in full

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** An NCCI PTP modifier indicator of '1' means a modifier is allowed to bypass the edit when documentation supports a distinct service. Why the others are wrong: **B** an indicator of '0' is the one that never allows a modifier override; **C** an edit does not require codes to be billed together—it restricts billing them together; **D** the column-two (component) code is the one denied unless the edit is appropriately overridden.

questions.stem: Under HIPAA, the 'minimum necessary' standard requires that a covered entity:

options.text: Limit the use, disclosure, and request of PHI to the least amount needed to accomplish the intended purpose
Disclose all of a patient's record whenever any portion is requested
Obtain written authorization before any treatment is provided
Retain records for a minimum of 25 years

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** The minimum necessary standard limits PHI use, disclosure, and requests to the least amount required for the purpose. Why the others are wrong: **B** disclosing the entire record regardless of need violates the standard; **C** treatment disclosures among providers generally do not require separate authorization, and minimum necessary does not even apply to treatment disclosures; **D** record-retention periods are set by other rules, not the minimum necessary standard.

questions.stem: A coder is pressured to assign a higher-level service code than the documentation supports to increase reimbursement. Reporting codes at a higher level than documented is known as:

options.text: Upcoding, which can constitute fraud under the False Claims Act
Unbundling, which is always permitted
Downcoding, a compliant conservative practice
Bundling, a routine NCCI function

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Reporting a higher level than the documentation supports is upcoding, a form of fraud that can trigger False Claims Act liability. Why the others are wrong: **B** unbundling (billing components separately to inflate payment) is improper, not always permitted; **C** downcoding means reporting a lower level and is not what is described; **D** bundling combines services and is a normal edit function, not the misconduct described.

questions.stem: A chart note describes a finding on the 'ventral' surface of the trunk. Ventral is synonymous with which directional term?

options.text: Anterior (toward the front of the body)
Posterior (toward the back of the body)
Superior (toward the head)
Distal (away from the trunk)

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Ventral and anterior both mean toward the front of the body. Why the others are wrong: **B** posterior (the back) is the synonym of dorsal, the opposite of ventral; **C** superior means toward the head, an unrelated axis; **D** distal describes a limb position relative to its attachment, not the front/back axis.

questions.stem: An operative report uses the suffix '-pexy' (as in 'orchiopexy'). What surgical action does -pexy describe?

options.text: Surgical crushing of a structure
Surgical fixation or suspension of an organ in place
Visual examination of an organ
Breakdown or dissolution of tissue

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** The suffix -pexy means surgical fixation or suspension (orchiopexy fixes an undescended testis in the scrotum). Why the others are wrong: **A** surgical crushing is -tripsy; **C** visual examination is -scopy; **D** breakdown or dissolution is -lysis.

questions.stem: Which two statements correctly describe components of the cardiovascular system relevant to coding? (Select two.)

options.text: Arteries carry blood away from the heart
The pericardium is the innermost lining in direct contact with the blood
The myocardium is the muscular middle layer of the heart wall
Veins always carry oxygen-rich blood

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, C):** Arteries carry blood away from the heart, and the myocardium is the muscular middle layer of the heart wall. Why the others are wrong: **B** the innermost lining in contact with blood is the endocardium, while the pericardium is the outer sac; **D** veins generally carry oxygen-poor blood (the pulmonary veins are the notable exception), so 'always' is false.

questions.stem: A pathophysiology note distinguishes a 'benign' from a 'malignant' neoplasm. The defining feature of a malignant neoplasm is that it:

options.text: Remains encapsulated and never recurs after removal
Is always smaller than a benign growth
Invades surrounding tissue and can metastasize to distant sites
Grows only within the epithelial layer and cannot spread

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** Malignant neoplasms invade adjacent tissue and have the capacity to metastasize to distant sites. Why the others are wrong: **A** staying encapsulated and non-recurrent describes benign behavior; **B** size does not determine malignancy; **D** confinement to the epithelium without spread describes carcinoma in situ, not invasive malignancy.

questions.stem: In ICD-10-CM, an 'Excludes1' note appearing under a code instructs the coder that:

options.text: The excluded condition is not part of this code but may be coded together if both are present
An additional code is always required
The code may only be used as a secondary diagnosis
The two conditions are mutually exclusive and cannot be coded together for the same encounter

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** Excludes1 is a 'pure' exclusion meaning the two codes represent mutually exclusive conditions and are not reported together. Why the others are wrong: **A** describes Excludes2, where both conditions may coexist and be coded together; **B** a mandatory additional code is signaled by 'Use additional code,' not Excludes1; **C** Excludes1 says nothing about primary versus secondary sequencing.

questions.stem: A patient is admitted for chemotherapy administration for a known malignancy and receives no other treatment that encounter. Per ICD-10-CM guidelines, the first-listed (principal) diagnosis should be:

options.text: The encounter-for-chemotherapy Z code (Z51.-), with the malignancy coded secondarily
The malignancy code first, with no Z code reported
A symptom code such as nausea
A personal-history-of-cancer Z code

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** When an encounter is solely for chemotherapy, the encounter-for-antineoplastic-chemotherapy Z code is sequenced first and the malignancy is listed secondarily. Why the others are wrong: **B** the malignancy is reported but not first when admission is only for the therapy; **C** a symptom is not the reason for the encounter here; **D** personal-history-of-cancer codes apply only after the malignancy is eradicated and no longer being treated.

questions.stem: In the ICD-10-CM Alphabetic Index, a term shown in parentheses immediately after a main term is a 'nonessential modifier.' This means the parenthetical word:

options.text: Must be documented or the code cannot be used
Does not have to be present in the documentation to assign the code
Changes the code to a different chapter
Indicates a mandatory seventh character

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** Nonessential modifiers appear in parentheses and supplement the main term but are not required to be documented for the code to apply. Why the others are wrong: **A** subterms that must be present are essential modifiers, listed indented, not in parentheses; **C** a nonessential modifier does not redirect the code to another chapter; **D** seventh-character requirements are shown in the Tabular List, not signaled by parentheses.

questions.stem: In the integumentary section, CPT distinguishes destruction of a lesion (e.g., by cryosurgery or electrosurgery) from excision primarily because destruction:

options.text: Always requires a layered closure
Is sized by adding margins to the lesion just as excision is
Ablates tissue without producing a specimen for measured excised-diameter sizing
Can only be performed on malignant lesions

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** Destruction ablates the lesion (cryo, electro, laser, chemical) without excising a measurable specimen, so it is not sized by excised diameter the way excision is. Why the others are wrong: **A** destruction typically needs no closure since no incision is made; **B** the excised-diameter + margin method applies to excision, not destruction; **D** destruction codes exist for both benign and malignant lesions.

questions.stem: When coding skin debridement in the integumentary section, the codes are selected based on the deepest tissue removed and the:

options.text: Length of the longest wound in centimeters
Patient's body mass index
Number of dressings applied afterward
Surface area (square centimeters) of the tissue debrided

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** Debridement codes are chosen by the deepest layer removed (e.g., subcutaneous tissue, muscle/fascia, bone) and the total surface area in square centimeters. Why the others are wrong: **A** linear wound length sizes repairs, not debridement; **B** BMI is irrelevant to debridement code selection; **C** dressing count plays no role in choosing the code.

questions.stem: A surgeon performs an arthrodesis. Based on the procedure name, an arthrodesis is the:

options.text: Surgical fusion of a joint
Surgical replacement of a joint with a prosthesis
Incision into a joint to drain fluid
Visual examination inside a joint

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Arthr/o (joint) + -desis (binding/fusion) means surgical fusion of a joint. Why the others are wrong: **B** prosthetic joint replacement is arthroplasty; **C** incising a joint to drain it is arthrotomy/arthrocentesis; **D** visual examination of a joint is arthroscopy.

questions.stem: In CPT musculoskeletal coding, application of the first cast or strapping during the initial care of a fracture by the treating physician is generally:

options.text: Always reported separately in addition to the fracture-care code
Included in the fracture-care code and not separately reported
Reported only with an anesthesia code
Never reported under any circumstance, even for a later replacement cast

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** The initial cast/strapping applied as part of the first fracture treatment is bundled into the fracture-care code. Why the others are wrong: **A** the first application is not separate when fracture-care is billed; **C** anesthesia does not govern whether the casting is reported; **D** a later replacement cast (e.g., during follow-up) can be separately reported, so 'never under any circumstance' is false.

questions.stem: Procedures of the urinary system, male and female genital systems, and maternity care are organized in which CPT Surgery numeric series?

options.text: The 30000 series
The 40000 series
The 50000 series
The 60000 series

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** The 50000 series covers urinary, male/female genital, and maternity care and delivery procedures. Why the others are wrong: **A** the 30000 series is respiratory, cardiovascular, and hemic/lymphatic; **B** the 40000 series is the digestive system; **D** the 60000 series is the endocrine, nervous, eye, and auditory systems.

questions.stem: In the respiratory section, a bronchoscopy code descriptor states it is 'with or without fluoroscopic guidance.' This phrasing tells the coder that:

options.text: Fluoroscopy must always be billed with a separate radiology code
The procedure cannot be performed without fluoroscopy
A modifier 26 is always required for the bronchoscopy
Fluoroscopic guidance, when used, is included in the code and not billed separately

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** When a descriptor says 'with or without' a service, that service is bundled into the code whether or not it is used, so it is not separately reported. Why the others are wrong: **A** separate billing would unbundle an included service; **B** 'with or without' explicitly allows the procedure to be done either way; **C** modifier 26 splits a professional/technical service and is not mandated here.

questions.stem: In the cardiovascular surgery section, selective catheter placement is coded based on the principle that the coder reports:

options.text: The most selective (farthest/highest-order) vessel catheterized in a given vascular family, not every vessel passed through
Each individual vessel the catheter passes through as a separate code
Only the access site where the needle entered
The least selective point reached in the vascular family

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** For catheter placement, you code the highest order (most selective) vessel entered within a vascular family; the intervening vessels are not separately reported. Why the others are wrong: **B** coding every traversed vessel overstates the service; **C** the puncture/access site alone does not capture selective placement; **D** reporting the least selective point understates the work performed.

questions.stem: Which two statements correctly describe how 'separate procedure' designations work in the CPT surgery section? (Select two.)

options.text: A 'separate procedure' must always be billed in addition to the primary procedure
A procedure labeled 'separate procedure' is not reported when it is an integral part of a larger procedure performed at the same session
The 'separate procedure' label means the code is an add-on code
A 'separate procedure' may be reported when it is performed independently or is unrelated/distinct from other services that day

questions.explanation: **Correct (B, D):** A 'separate procedure' is bundled when it is a component of a larger procedure done the same session, but it may be reported when performed alone or as a distinct, unrelated service (often with modifier 59). Why the others are wrong: **A** it is not always billed separately—when integral to a larger service it is bundled; **C** 'separate procedure' is unrelated to the add-on (+) designation.

questions.stem: A note documents a 'cholecystectomy.' Based on the term's components, this is removal of the:

options.text: Common bile duct
Gallbladder
Colon
Bladder (urinary)

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** Chol/e (bile) + cyst (sac/bladder) + -ectomy (removal) = removal of the gallbladder. Why the others are wrong: **A** the common bile duct relates to choledoch/o terms; **C** colon removal is colectomy; **D** removal of the urinary bladder is cystectomy (without the chol/e root).

questions.stem: During one operative session a surgeon performs a primary procedure and a second, lesser procedure through the same incision. To indicate the additional procedure(s) beyond the primary in a physician (non-facility) claim, the coder generally appends to the secondary code:

options.text: Modifier 50 (bilateral)
Modifier 25 (significant, separate E/M)
Modifier 51 (multiple procedures)
Modifier 91 (repeat lab test)

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** Modifier 51 identifies that multiple procedures were performed at the same session by the same provider, appended to the secondary/lesser procedures. Why the others are wrong: **A** modifier 50 reports a bilateral procedure, not multiple different procedures; **B** modifier 25 applies to E/M services, not surgical multiplicity; **D** modifier 91 is for repeated clinical lab tests.

questions.stem: A staged or related procedure by the same physician during the postoperative period (planned prospectively at the time of the first surgery) is reported with which modifier?

options.text: Modifier 78
Modifier 79
Modifier 76
Modifier 58

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** Modifier 58 reports a staged, planned, or more extensive related procedure performed by the same physician during the global period. Why the others are wrong: **A** modifier 78 is an unplanned return to the OR for a complication; **B** modifier 79 is an unrelated procedure during the global period; **C** modifier 76 is a repeat of the same procedure by the same physician, not a staged service.

questions.stem: Two surgeons of different specialties each perform a distinct part of the same operation, each acting as a primary surgeon for their portion. Each surgeon reports the procedure code with:

options.text: Modifier 62 (two surgeons / co-surgeons)
Modifier 80 (assistant surgeon)
Modifier 66 (surgical team)
Modifier 82 (assistant surgeon when a qualified resident is unavailable)

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Modifier 62 is used when two surgeons work together as primary surgeons, each performing a distinct part of the same procedure. Why the others are wrong: **B** modifier 80 designates an assistant surgeon, not a co-primary; **C** modifier 66 is for a larger surgical team (often three or more surgeons); **D** modifier 82 is an assistant-surgeon modifier used when no qualified resident is available.

questions.stem: In the female genital/maternity subsection, a procedure described as performed 'transvaginally' refers to an approach through the:

options.text: Abdominal wall
Vagina
Rectum
Umbilicus via laparoscope

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** 'Transvaginal' means the approach is through the vagina. Why the others are wrong: **A** through the abdominal wall is a transabdominal/open approach; **C** through the rectum is transrectal; **D** through the umbilicus with a scope is a laparoscopic approach.

questions.stem: In the nervous system subsection, CPT codes for spinal procedures often reference the number of 'interspaces' or 'vertebral segments.' An 'interspace' refers to:

options.text: A single vertebral bone in isolation
The spinal cord segment only
The non-bony space between two adjacent vertebral bodies (the disc space)
The space between the skull and the first rib

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** An interspace is the non-bony intervertebral space (the disc space) between two adjacent vertebral bodies. Why the others are wrong: **A** a single vertebral bone is a vertebral segment, a different counting unit; **B** the cord segment is neural tissue, not the disc interspace; **D** that region is unrelated to spinal interspace terminology.

questions.stem: A procedure on the eye is documented as performed on the 'adnexa.' The ocular adnexa include structures such as the:

options.text: Retina and optic nerve only
Cornea and lens only
Inner ear structures
Eyelids, lacrimal apparatus, and extraocular muscles

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** The ocular adnexa are the accessory structures around the eye—the eyelids, lacrimal (tear) apparatus, conjunctiva, and extraocular muscles. Why the others are wrong: **A** the retina and optic nerve are part of the eyeball (globe), not the adnexa; **B** the cornea and lens are also components of the globe itself; **C** the inner ear is part of the auditory system, not the ocular adnexa.

questions.stem: In E/M coding, the distinction between a 'new patient' and an 'established patient' generally turns on whether the patient has received professional services from the physician or another physician of the same specialty and group within:

options.text: The past three years
The past six months
The past one year
The patient's lifetime

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** A new patient is one who has not received face-to-face professional services from the physician (or same-specialty, same-group physician) within the prior three years. Why the others are wrong: **B** six months is not the CPT threshold; **C** one year is not the threshold; **D** a lifetime look-back would make almost no one 'new,' which is not the rule.

questions.stem: A physician documents that a 'consultation' was requested by another physician for advice on a patient's problem, and a written report was returned to the requesting provider. The key feature that distinguishes a consultation from a transfer of care is that a consultation involves:

options.text: The consultant immediately assuming full responsibility for all of the patient's care
A request for opinion/advice with a report back, while the requesting provider retains management
No communication back to the requesting provider
A self-referral by the patient with no requesting provider

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** A consultation is rendered at another provider's request for opinion or advice, with findings communicated back, and the requesting provider continues to manage the patient. Why the others are wrong: **A** assuming full management is a transfer of care, not a consult; **C** a report back to the requestor is a defining element of a consultation; **D** a patient self-referral without a requesting provider is not a consultation.

questions.stem: A physician makes the decision to perform major surgery (90-day global) during an E/M visit on the day before the surgery. The E/M service is reported with which modifier?

options.text: Modifier 25 (significant, separate E/M with a minor procedure)
Modifier 24 (unrelated E/M in the postoperative period)
Modifier 57 (decision for surgery)
Modifier 58 (staged procedure)

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** Modifier 57 identifies the E/M visit at which the decision for major (typically 90-day global) surgery was made, on the day of or day before the procedure. Why the others are wrong: **A** modifier 25 is for a separate E/M on the same day as a minor procedure; **B** modifier 24 applies to an unrelated E/M during the postoperative period; **D** modifier 58 is for a staged surgical procedure, not an E/M.

questions.stem: Which two services are part of the CPT-defined anesthesia package and therefore not separately reported by the anesthesiologist? (Select two.)

options.text: The usual pre-anesthetic evaluation of the patient
Placement of a separately reportable invasive arterial or central venous line for monitoring
Postoperative management of an unrelated chronic pain condition in clinic
Routine intraoperative monitoring (e.g., ECG, pulse oximetry, blood pressure)

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, D):** The anesthesia package includes the usual preoperative and postoperative visits and routine monitoring such as ECG, pulse oximetry, and blood pressure. Why the others are wrong: **B** placement of an invasive line (arterial or central venous) for monitoring is separately reportable; **C** managing an unrelated chronic pain problem in clinic is a distinct service, not part of the anesthesia package.

questions.stem: In anesthesia coding, qualifying circumstances codes (e.g., for extreme age, emergency conditions, or total body hypothermia) are best described as:

options.text: Stand-alone anesthesia codes that replace the primary anesthesia code
Physical status modifiers appended to the surgery code
ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes for the underlying condition
Add-on codes reported in addition to the primary anesthesia code to reflect difficult circumstances

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** Qualifying circumstances are add-on codes reported with the primary anesthesia code to capture conditions that significantly increase the difficulty of anesthesia (extreme age, emergency, hypothermia, controlled hypotension). Why the others are wrong: **A** they supplement, not replace, the primary anesthesia code; **B** physical status (P1-P6) is a separate modifier set; **C** they are CPT add-on codes, not ICD-10-CM diagnoses.

questions.stem: In CPT Radiology, the diagnostic ultrasound term 'B-scan' (B-mode) refers to a display that shows:

options.text: A two-dimensional image of tissues and organ structures
A one-dimensional amplitude trace along a single line
Only blood-flow velocity with no anatomic image
A radioactive tracer distribution

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** B-scan (B-mode, brightness mode) produces a two-dimensional image of the tissues and organ anatomy. Why the others are wrong: **B** a one-dimensional amplitude trace describes A-mode ultrasound; **C** flow velocity alone describes Doppler, not B-mode; **D** a radioactive tracer distribution describes nuclear medicine, not ultrasound.

questions.stem: A nuclear medicine study is performed in which a radiopharmaceutical is administered to image organ function. For coding, the radiopharmaceutical (the diagnostic radionuclide itself) is generally:

options.text: Always bundled into the imaging code and never separately reported
Reported separately from the imaging procedure code, often with a HCPCS supply code
Coded as an E/M service
Reported only as an ICD-10-CM code

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** In nuclear medicine, the imaging procedure and the radiopharmaceutical/radionuclide supply are typically reported separately, the supply often via a HCPCS code. Why the others are wrong: **A** the radiopharmaceutical is generally a separately reportable supply, not always bundled; **C** the agent is a supply, not an E/M service; **D** ICD-10-CM codes capture diagnoses, not the radiopharmaceutical supply.

questions.stem: In the Pathology and Laboratory section, a CPT 'panel' code (organ- or disease-oriented panel) may be reported only when:

options.text: At least one component test in the panel was performed
The physician orders the panel by name, regardless of which tests run
All of the individual tests listed as components of that panel were performed
Any tests from any panel are combined to reach the count

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** An organ- or disease-oriented panel code is reported only when every component test that defines the panel is performed. Why the others are wrong: **A** performing just one component does not meet the panel definition; **B** the order name alone is insufficient—the listed tests must actually be done; **D** components cannot be mixed across different panels to assemble one.

questions.stem: In the Medicine section, therapeutic drug infusion and injection codes use a hierarchy of 'initial' versus 'sequential/concurrent' services. Per CPT, when a single encounter has multiple infusions, the 'initial' code is generally assigned to the:

options.text: Last infusion completed during the visit
Shortest infusion regardless of purpose
Each and every infusion, since all are 'initial'
Primary reason for the encounter (the key/primary service), not simply the first one started chronologically

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** For physician reporting, the 'initial' code reflects the primary/key reason for the encounter, even if another substance was infused first in time. Why the others are wrong: **A** the last infusion is not automatically the initial service; **B** infusion duration does not determine the initial designation; **C** only one initial service is reported per encounter (per the hierarchy), with others as sequential/concurrent.

questions.stem: A patient who has not received face-to-face care has a brief check-in (a 'virtual check-in') and, in a separate scenario, undergoes physical therapy where the therapist provides one-on-one services in 15-minute units. These therapy codes are an example of:

options.text: Time-based (per-unit) codes governed by the CPT/Medicare '8-minute' style midpoint rules for counting units
Untimed service codes reported once per day regardless of duration
Add-on codes that cannot be reported without a surgery
Anesthesia base-unit codes

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Constant-attendance, one-on-one therapy services are time-based and counted in 15-minute units using midpoint ('8-minute') threshold rules to determine billable units. Why the others are wrong: **B** untimed (service-based) PT codes are reported once per session, which is the opposite category; **C** these are not surgical add-on codes; **D** anesthesia base units are a different valuation system entirely.

questions.stem: In CPT, a 'category III' code is best described as a code that is:

options.text: A permanent five-digit numeric procedure code
A temporary set of codes for emerging technologies, services, and procedures, formatted with a terminal letter T
A supplemental performance-measurement tracking code
A HCPCS Level II national code

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** Category III codes are temporary codes for emerging technologies and services, written with four digits plus a terminal 'T.' Why the others are wrong: **A** permanent five-digit numeric procedure codes are Category I; **C** performance-measurement tracking codes are Category II (ending in F); **D** HCPCS Level II national codes are a separate alphanumeric code set, not CPT Category III.

questions.stem: Arrange these office/outpatient E/M medical decision making (MDM) complexity levels in ascending order, from lowest to highest.

options.text: Straightforward
Low complexity
Moderate complexity
High complexity

questions.explanation: The correct ascending order of MDM is straightforward, then low, then moderate, then high complexity. This sequence matters because the office/outpatient E/M level is driven by MDM (or time): a higher MDM level requires meeting the threshold in at least two of the three MDM elements (problems, data, risk), so a coder must know the ladder to map documentation to the correct level of service.

questions.stem: A drug-related HCPCS J code descriptor specifies a dosage of 'per 10 mg.' If 30 mg of the drug is administered, the coder should generally report:

options.text: One unit of the J code
Thirty units of the J code
Three units of the J code
One-third of a unit of the J code

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** When the code represents 'per 10 mg,' a 30 mg dose equals three billable units (30 ÷ 10). Why the others are wrong: **A** one unit would represent only 10 mg, under-reporting the dose; **B** thirty units would mean the descriptor was per 1 mg, which it is not; **D** fractional units misapply the per-10-mg increment.

questions.stem: On a Medicare claim, the HCPCS modifiers GA, GX, GY, and GZ are associated with:

options.text: Laterality of a paired organ
Professional versus technical component splits
Anesthesia physical status
Advance Beneficiary Notice (ABN) status and statutory non-coverage of an item or service

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** The G-series waiver modifiers relate to ABN and coverage: GA (waiver on file, expected denial), GX (voluntary ABN for non-covered item), GY (statutorily excluded/not a benefit), and GZ (expected denial, no ABN obtained). Why the others are wrong: **A** laterality uses LT/RT; **B** professional/technical splits use 26/TC; **C** anesthesia physical status uses P1-P6.

questions.stem: In CPT, a parenthetical instruction that reads '(Do not report 12345 in conjunction with 67890)' is best understood as:

options.text: A code-pairing exclusion telling the coder those two codes may not be reported together for the same encounter
A suggestion that the two codes are usually billed together
An instruction to always append modifier 50
A note that the first code has been deleted

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** A 'Do not report X in conjunction with Y' parenthetical is an exclusionary code-pairing instruction barring those codes from being billed together on the same encounter. Why the others are wrong: **B** it forbids, rather than encourages, billing them together; **C** it does not address bilateral modifier 50; **D** a deleted code would be shown by deletion notation, not this conjunction instruction.

questions.stem: When abstracting an operative report into CPT and ICD-10-CM codes, which two practices reflect correct coding from documentation? (Select two.)

options.text: Assume an unstated approach (open vs. laparoscopic) based on what is most commonly done
Code the definitive postoperative diagnosis over the preoperative diagnosis when the pathology/findings differ
Assign codes only for procedures actually documented as performed, not those merely planned
Code from the surgeon's verbal estimate given outside the medical record

questions.explanation: **Correct (B, C):** The confirmed postoperative diagnosis takes precedence when it differs from the preoperative impression, and only documented, actually-performed procedures are coded. Why the others are wrong: **A** the coder may not assume an approach that is not documented—query the provider instead; **D** coding from verbal estimates outside the record is not supported documentation.

questions.stem: A clinic submits a claim for a service that is not reasonable and necessary for the patient's condition. The Medicare requirement that a service be appropriate for the diagnosis and meet accepted standards of care is the principle of:

options.text: Minimum necessary
Medical necessity
Assignment of benefits
Coordination of benefits

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** Medical necessity requires that services be reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis or treatment and meet accepted standards. Why the others are wrong: **A** 'minimum necessary' is a HIPAA privacy standard limiting PHI disclosure, not a coverage standard; **C** assignment of benefits concerns who is paid; **D** coordination of benefits determines payer order when multiple plans exist.

questions.stem: The federal statute that prohibits knowingly offering, paying, soliciting, or receiving remuneration to induce referrals of items or services payable by a federal health care program is the:

options.text: Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA)
Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health (HITECH) Act
Anti-Kickback Statute
Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA)

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** The Anti-Kickback Statute criminalizes knowingly paying or receiving remuneration to induce referrals for items/services reimbursable by federal health care programs. Why the others are wrong: **A** EMTALA governs emergency screening and stabilization regardless of ability to pay; **B** HITECH strengthens HIPAA privacy/security and breach rules; **D** FMLA concerns employee job-protected leave, unrelated to referral remuneration.

questions.stem: A pathology report describes a lesion using the suffix '-oma.' This suffix indicates the finding is a:

options.text: Inflammation
Tumor or mass
Abnormal condition of hardening
Discharge or flow

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** The suffix -oma means a tumor or mass (e.g., lip/oma is a fatty tumor). Why the others are wrong: **A** inflammation is -itis; **C** an abnormal condition of hardening is -sclerosis; **D** a discharge or flow is -rrhea.

questions.stem: An imaging order requests a view in the 'transverse' (axial) plane. This plane divides the body into:

options.text: Right and left portions
Anterior and posterior (front and back) portions
Superior and inferior (upper and lower) portions
Internal and external portions

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** The transverse (axial) plane is a horizontal cut dividing the body into superior (upper) and inferior (lower) portions. Why the others are wrong: **A** a sagittal plane divides into right and left portions; **B** a coronal (frontal) plane divides into anterior and posterior portions; **D** no standard anatomical plane divides into internal and external portions.

questions.stem: A nephrology note references the 'functional unit' of the kidney responsible for filtering blood and forming urine. This structure is the:

options.text: Alveolus
Hepatocyte
Sarcomere
Nephron

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** The nephron is the microscopic functional unit of the kidney where filtration and urine formation occur. Why the others are wrong: **A** the alveolus is the gas-exchange unit of the lung; **B** the hepatocyte is the functional liver cell; **C** the sarcomere is the contractile unit of skeletal muscle.

questions.stem: Which two pairings correctly match a body cavity with an organ it contains? (Select two.)

options.text: Thoracic cavity — the heart and lungs
Cranial cavity — the urinary bladder
Pelvic cavity — the urinary bladder and rectum
Spinal cavity — the stomach

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, C):** The thoracic cavity houses the heart and lungs, and the pelvic cavity contains the urinary bladder and rectum. Why the others are wrong: **B** the cranial cavity holds the brain, not the bladder; **D** the spinal (vertebral) cavity holds the spinal cord, while the stomach is in the abdominal cavity.

questions.stem: In the ICD-10-CM Alphabetic Index, the abbreviation 'NEC' next to a term tells the coder that:

options.text: The information needed to assign a more specific code is missing from the record
No additional code may be assigned
A more specific code is unavailable, so an 'other specified' code is used because the documented condition has no distinct code
The code requires a seventh character

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** 'NEC' (not elsewhere classifiable) means the condition is specified but the classification has no distinct code, so an 'other specified' code is assigned. Why the others are wrong: **A** describes 'NOS' (not otherwise specified), an unspecified-code situation; **B** NEC does not bar additional codes; **D** seventh-character requirements are shown in the Tabular List, unrelated to NEC.

questions.stem: A patient presents with acute abdominal pain. After workup the physician documents 'rule out appendicitis' but no condition is confirmed at this outpatient encounter. Per ICD-10-CM outpatient guidelines, the coder should report:

options.text: The confirmed appendicitis code
The signs/symptoms documented (e.g., the abdominal pain), not the uncertain 'rule out' diagnosis
The 'rule out' diagnosis as if it were confirmed
A personal-history code for appendicitis

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** In the outpatient setting, uncertain diagnoses ('rule out,' 'probable,' 'suspected') are not coded; the documented signs and symptoms are reported instead. Why the others are wrong: **A** nothing was confirmed, so the disease code is not assigned; **C** coding an uncertain diagnosis as confirmed is prohibited for outpatient encounters; **D** there is no history of a condition that never existed.

questions.stem: A diabetic patient is seen for a diabetic foot ulcer. ICD-10-CM provides a single code capturing both the diabetes and the ulcer relationship. This type of code is called a:

options.text: Placeholder code
Manifestation-only code
Z code
Combination code

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** A combination code is a single code that classifies two diagnoses, or a diagnosis with an associated manifestation or complication, such as diabetes with a specified complication. Why the others are wrong: **A** a placeholder is the 'X' dummy character within a code; **B** a manifestation-only code cannot be sequenced first and is paired with an etiology, unlike a single combination code; **C** Z codes capture factors/status, not a disease-with-complication pairing.

questions.stem: In the integumentary section, a 'shaving' of an epidermal or dermal lesion is distinguished from an excision because shaving is:

options.text: Always a full-thickness removal requiring layered closure
Performed only on subcutaneous masses
A horizontal or tangential removal that does not require full-thickness (through-the-dermis) excision or suture closure
Coded by the depth of muscle removed

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** Shaving is the sharp horizontal/tangential removal of a raised epidermal or dermal lesion without a full-thickness excision, and it does not require suture closure. Why the others are wrong: **A** full-thickness removal with closure describes excision, not shaving; **B** shaving addresses superficial skin lesions, not deep subcutaneous masses; **D** muscle depth governs debridement/musculoskeletal coding, not shaving.

questions.stem: When coding a skin graft, CPT distinguishes an 'autograft' from an 'allograft.' An autograft uses tissue that is:

options.text: Donated from another human (cadaver or living donor)
Harvested from the patient's own body
Derived from an animal source
Entirely synthetic/manufactured

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** An autograft transfers the patient's own tissue from one site to another. Why the others are wrong: **A** tissue donated from another human is an allograft (homograft); **C** tissue from an animal source is a xenograft; **D** fully synthetic material is a skin substitute/biologic dressing, not an autograft.

questions.stem: A surgeon performs an 'open reduction with internal fixation (ORIF)' of a fracture. The 'reduction' portion of this procedure refers to:

options.text: Removing a portion of the bone to shorten it
Decreasing the dose of anesthesia used
Restoring the fractured bone fragments to their normal anatomic alignment
Reducing the size of the surgical incision

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** Reduction means realigning (manipulating) the fracture fragments back into proper anatomic position; in ORIF the site is opened and hardware fixes the alignment. Why the others are wrong: **A** removing bone to shorten it is an ostectomy/osteotomy concept, not reduction; **B** reduction is unrelated to anesthesia dosing; **D** it does not refer to incision size.

questions.stem: In the musculoskeletal section, CPT defines coding for an 'excision' of a bone tumor differently depending on whether it is radical or not. The use of an allograft or autograft bone for the resulting defect is generally:

options.text: Reported separately in addition to the resection when the code descriptor does not already include the graft
Never separately reportable under any circumstance
Reported only as an E/M service
Coded with anesthesia time units

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** When a bone graft (allograft or autograft) is obtained/placed and the resection code does not already bundle it, the graft is separately reportable. Why the others are wrong: **B** 'never reportable' is wrong because separate graft codes exist when not bundled; **C** a bone graft is a surgical service, not E/M; **D** it is not valued by anesthesia time units.

questions.stem: A patient undergoes a 'lobectomy' of the lung. Based on the procedure name, this is removal of:

options.text: An entire lung
A small wedge of lung tissue only
The lining around the lung
One lobe of the lung

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** A lobectomy is removal of a single lobe of the lung. Why the others are wrong: **A** removal of an entire lung is a pneumonectomy; **B** removal of a small wedge of tissue is a wedge resection; **C** removal of the pleural lining is a pleurectomy.

questions.stem: In the cardiovascular surgery section, coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) procedures are divided into venous-only grafts, arterial grafts, and combined arterial-venous grafts. When both an arterial graft and a venous graft are performed in the same CABG, the coding rule is to report:

options.text: A combined arterial-venous grafting code together with the appropriate arterial grafting code, per the CABG guidelines
Only the venous graft code, ignoring the arterial graft
Only an E/M code for the encounter
A single unrelated cardiology consult code

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** CPT's CABG guidelines instruct that when arterial and venous grafts are combined, you report a combined arterial-venous grafting code along with the appropriate arterial grafting code. Why the others are wrong: **B** reporting only the venous graft ignores documented arterial grafting; **C** CABG is a surgical procedure, not an E/M service; **D** a consult code does not describe the bypass surgery performed.

questions.stem: Which two statements about the hemic and lymphatic subsection of CPT Surgery are correct? (Select two.)

options.text: A 'lymphadenectomy' is the surgical removal of lymph node(s)
A 'splenectomy' is removal of the spleen
A 'splenectomy' is removal of the thymus
A 'lymphadenectomy' is an incision into a vein

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, B):** A lymphadenectomy removes lymph node(s) and a splenectomy removes the spleen. Why the others are wrong: **C** removal of the thymus is a thymectomy, not a splenectomy; **D** an incision into a vein is a venotomy/phlebotomy, not a lymphadenectomy.

questions.stem: A gastroenterologist performs an EGD (esophagogastroduodenoscopy). Based on the term, this endoscopy examines the:

options.text: Colon and rectum
Esophagus, stomach, and duodenum
Bile ducts and pancreatic duct
Trachea and bronchi

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** Esophag/o + gastr/o + duoden/o + -scopy means visualization of the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum. Why the others are wrong: **A** the colon and rectum are examined by colonoscopy; **C** the bile and pancreatic ducts are examined by ERCP; **D** the trachea and bronchi are examined by bronchoscopy.

questions.stem: During a colonoscopy, the physician removes one polyp by snare technique and a separate, distinct polyp by cold biopsy forceps at a different site. CPT guidance for reporting multiple endoscopic lesion-removal techniques in the same session is to:

options.text: Report each distinct removal technique separately, appending modifier 59 (or an X{EPSU} modifier) to the additional technique to show it was a distinct service
Report only the single most extensive technique and bundle the rest
Report each technique but never use any modifier
Report an E/M visit instead of the procedures

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** When different removal techniques are used on separate lesions, each technique is reported, and modifier 59 (or an appropriate X{EPSU} modifier) marks the additional technique as a distinct procedural service. Why the others are wrong: **B** distinct techniques on different lesions are not all bundled into one; **C** without a distinct-service modifier the additional technique may be denied as bundled; **D** an E/M does not capture the polypectomy work.

questions.stem: A urologist performs a 'transurethral resection of the prostate' (TURP). The approach in this procedure is through the:

options.text: Lower abdominal wall
Urethra
Perineum
Rectum

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** 'Transurethral' means the resection is performed through the urethra using a resectoscope. Why the others are wrong: **A** a suprapubic/retropubic prostatectomy goes through the lower abdomen; **C** a perineal prostatectomy is through the perineum; **D** a transrectal approach is through the rectum, not used for TURP.

questions.stem: An NCCI Procedure-to-Procedure edit bundles a 'Column 2' (component) code into a 'Column 1' (comprehensive) code. When the edit applies and no override is appropriate, the result is that the:

options.text: Column 1 comprehensive code is payable and the Column 2 component code is denied as bundled
Column 2 code is payable and the Column 1 code is denied
Both codes are always paid in full
Both codes are always denied

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** In a PTP edit, the Column 1 (comprehensive) code is the payable service and the Column 2 (component) code is denied as bundled unless an appropriate modifier overrides the edit. Why the others are wrong: **B** the column-two component code is the one denied, not the comprehensive code; **C** the edit exists precisely to prevent paying both together; **D** the comprehensive Column 1 code remains payable, so 'both denied' is wrong.
